lesson.title: AI and the work of tomorrow
lesson.subtitle: Tasks change, new work appears, and the skills to build

video.title: AI and the work of tomorrow
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — teacher educator from Bangladesh, visiting the school’s AI club (main character)
Mr Okafor — science teacher who runs the school’s AI club (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer, speaking to the student)

chapters.label: Will AI take my mum’s job?
AI work, skills and the lab

scenes.visual: The AI club, the day after. A sticky note on the whiteboard in a student’s handwriting: ‘Will AI take my mum’s job?’, with a small drawing of a nurse’s cap. Dr Farah taps the note and turns to the group, serious but kind.
scenes.animation: The sticky note flutters onto the board (200 ms); Dr Farah turns; gentle push-in.
scenes.narration: Yesterday, one of you asked me a big question. “Will AI take my mum’s job?” She’s a nurse. Let’s find an honest answer: no hype, and no fear.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey card. The Darsi mark pops in, then the course name, the lesson title and a yellow ‘AI’ track chip with the spark icon.
scenes.animation: Mark scales 0→100% with a small overshoot (≤ 200 ms); title slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: AI and the work of tomorrow
scenes.narration: Today: how AI changes work, the new work it creates, and skills worth building.

scenes.visual: A nurse in a clinic, surrounded by task cards: checking a patient, writing notes, talking with a family. Two cards get a small robot helper badge (spoken notes becoming text on a tablet; a warning light on a monitor). The card of the nurse calming a frightened child gets a heart and no badge.
scenes.animation: Task cards fan out around the nurse; helper badges pop on two cards (150 ms); the heart pulses once.
scenes.narration: A job is a bundle of tasks. A nurse checks patients, writes notes and talks with families. AI can help with some: turning speech into notes, or flagging a worrying reading. It can’t calm a frightened child. So AI usually changes tasks, not whole jobs.

scenes.visual: A balance: on one side a few task cards fade (a typist’s desk, a pile of forms). On the other, new figures appear: a young woman at a laptop tagging photos of cassava leaves and a man transcribing a voice recording with headphones; an engineer at a whiteboard; a tester ticking a checklist.
scenes.animation: Faded cards drift down; new figures pop in one by one (200 ms each).
scenes.on_screen_text: Some work shrinks, new work grows
scenes.narration: Honestly, some jobs will shrink, and people will need new skills. But AI also creates work. Someone has to label data, like photos of sick crops or Hausa voice recordings: real work that deserves fair pay. Others build models, test them and fix them.

scenes.visual: Clean white card with the AI track chip, split in two. Left: a robot arm sorts envelopes into a ‘spam’ tray by itself. Right: a nurse looks at a monitor where a small AI alert lights up, and she decides what to do.
scenes.animation: Left half slides in, then the right; the alert light blinks once.
scenes.narration: Two words help here. Automation: AI does a task instead of a person, like sorting spam. Augmentation: AI helps a person do it better, like an alert for a nurse. Most changes mix the two.

scenes.visual: A busy market. A trader counts a thick pile of cash, then the scene changes: she takes payment on her phone in seconds and smiles. On the corner, a small kiosk with a ‘Mobile money agent’ sign, a queue in front. Dr Farah stands at the side of the frame.
scenes.animation: Cash pile shrinks into a phone (400 ms); the kiosk sign swings into place.
scenes.narration: Think of mobile money. Market traders didn’t disappear when it arrived. Counting cash took less time, and a new job appeared on every corner: the mobile money agent. AI is a bigger change, but often works the same way.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor pops in beside a hospital corridor, where a doctor speaks into a phone and words appear on a tablet. Three answer cards drop in below him.
scenes.animation: Character slides in from the side; answer cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A hospital starts using AI to turn doctors’ spoken notes into text. What’s most likely to happen?

scenes.visual: The card ‘Some of their tasks change’ gets a check badge. The doctor puts the tablet down and sits with a patient; behind her, a colleague reads the notes and corrects one highlighted word, a medicine dose.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops (150 ms); the highlighted dose flips to the corrected number.
scenes.narration: Some of their tasks change. Doctors type less and spend more time with patients. But someone still checks the notes, because AI can mishear a name or a dose.

scenes.visual: Four cards, about five seconds each: a farmer photographing a cassava leaf with a phone; a clinic worker looking at a chest X-ray with an AI highlight; a planner’s map of a town with bus routes and stops; a young person recording sentences in their language for voice typing.
scenes.animation: Each card flips in from the side as it is named. Keep motion simple and readable on a small screen.
scenes.narration: AI work is already near you. On farms, apps spot crop disease from leaf photos. In clinics, AI helps read X-rays. Planners use it to set bus routes. And people train voice typing for Yoruba, Swahili and Bangla.

scenes.visual: A student’s backpack opens and four skill badges fly out and pin themselves to the strap: a calculator with a small chart (maths and data), a magnifying glass (judging information), a balance scale (ethics), two hands meeting (working with people).
scenes.animation: Badges fly out on curved paths, one per sentence, and click into place (150 ms).
scenes.narration: So which skills should you build? Maths and data, to understand what AI does. Judging information, to check what it says. Ethics, to ask whether it should. And working with people, which no AI can do for you.

scenes.visual: A phone screen with the ‘Find groups (k-means)’ lab: a town map with small house marks and four big rings for bus stops. Lines join each house to its nearest stop; the rings slide to the middle of their houses, and four coloured neighbourhoods appear. A finger moves the ‘number of bus stops’ slider.
scenes.animation: Lines draw from houses to stops; stops glide to their new places in two rounds; the slider moves from 4 to 3.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: place the bus stops
scenes.narration: In the app, you’re the planner: place your school’s bus stops. Every house joins its nearest stop, every stop moves to the middle of its houses, and neighbourhoods appear by themselves. But you choose how many stops: a human decision.

scenes.visual: Dr Farah beside the skill badges from earlier. Two answer cards appear beside her.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. As AI spreads, which skill becomes more valuable: memorising facts, or judging whether information is true?

scenes.visual: The ‘Judging whether information is true’ card gets the check badge, then the screen resolves into a summary: task cards reshuffling, new figures (labeller, engineer, tester), and the four skill badges.
scenes.animation: Points tick in one by one; the takeaway bar rises last.
scenes.narration: Judging information: AI produces facts in seconds, but someone must check them. Remember: AI mostly changes tasks, not whole jobs. It creates new work too, from labelling data to testing. And build data skills, judgement, ethics and teamwork.

scenes.visual: Evening at home: a student with a notebook interviews an uncle who drives a minibus; then a quick cut to the student interviewing a market trader. In the notebook, two columns: ‘AI could help’ and ‘AI never should’. Dr Farah smiles at the side.
scenes.animation: Notebook columns fill in with handwriting; end card fades in.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: interview an adult about their work. Ask for one task AI could help with, and one it never should. Then ask them why, and write down what they say.

checkpoints.prompt: A hospital uses AI to turn doctors’ spoken notes into text. What’s most likely to happen?

options.text: Some of the doctors’ tasks change

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the AI takes over one task, typing notes, so the doctors’ work changes, but the job stays.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the AI takes over one task, typing notes. The doctors’ work changes, but they’re still needed, and someone must check the notes.

checkpoints.prompt: As AI spreads, which skill becomes more valuable?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — AI can produce facts in seconds, true or not. Someone has to judge them.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — AI can produce facts in seconds, and they can be wrong. Judging information is the skill that grows in value.
